requirements.requirement: The system shall automatically assess key stage 2 test administration applications (including compensatory spelling marks, additional time, timetable variations, and special considerations) against published business rules, auto-approving or auto-rejecting qualifying applications and routing unfulfilled or non-automated cases to operational staff for manual review.

The system shall send automated email notifications to applicant schools upon application updates and generate printable PDF outcome letters that detail the decision, including mandatory explicit written rationales for rejected applications.

The system shall provide audit capabilities that enable administrative staff to flag and quality-check a minimum 10% sample of auto-approved special consideration applications to verify decision accuracy and compliance.
The system shall provide a formal appeals workflow enabling schools to submit requests for decision reviews, which can be assigned to, reviewed by, and updated by a management team member.

The system shall enforce an annual data clear-down protocol that removes submitted application form instance data from the active environment every 12 months prior to opening the platform for the subsequent academic year.

The system shall support configurable date parameters, wording text, and decision logic for annual updates, allowing full verification in a isolated User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment prior to annual production release.
The system shall restrict supplier and administrative data access strictly to the data attributes required to perform contractually defined assessment operational tasks.

The system architecture shall implement a hub-and-spoke cloud infrastructure model that terminates all data ingress and egress in a central hub, prohibiting direct public internet access to back-end application and storage spokes.

The system shall implement multi-region data replication and database backup procedures to achieve a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of no more than 24 hours and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of no more than 4 hours in the event of a disaster.

The system shall provide automated load monitoring and peak traffic management (such as auto-scaling tiers and queue management integration) to maintain service availability during peak usage periods, such as test result return days.
The system shall dynamically select and deliver test items using an Item Response Theory (IRT) model that adjusts question difficulty based on the applicant's live response accuracy.
The system shall iteratively update the applicant's ability estimate (θ̂) after each submitted response using Expected A Posteriori (EAP) numerical integration across 33 quadrature points.
The system shall automatically terminate a test session when either the posterior standard error of measurement (SEθ) falls below 0.20 or the maximum predefined test length is reached.

The system shall implement exposure control algorithms (such as Randomesque selection) to prevent test items from exceeding defined exposure thresholds and ensure candidates do not see repeat questions.
The system shall provide applicants with introductory guidance explaining the adaptive test mechanism and present at least one non-scoring practice question before starting the evaluated test.

The system shall securely ingest pseudonymized candidate identifiers from Civil Service Jobs and return calculated test score parameters back to Civil Service Jobs and the Cabinet Office GRID database via an API.

The system shall evaluate calculated scores against predefined benchmark cut-scores to automatically mark scores below threshold as 'not passed' and pass successful applications to human hiring managers.

The system shall record full session execution logs—including candidate response vectors, item parameters, posterior standard errors, and random seeds—to support auditability and full simulation replay.
The system shall adhere to NCSC Cloud Security and Security Design Principles, ensuring continuous system availability (24/7 operational capability outside scheduled maintenance windows).
The system shall enforce data minimization by ensuring no protected sensitive demographic attributes are stored within the external psychometric test delivery platform.
The system shall provide the user with a practice test question that does not contribute to the final score prior to being scored.
